summary: All six tasks done in my three files (cat_impacts.py, cat_drive.py, cat_alarms.py). One build of the 11 sounds with CLAP and --describe: all 11 pass every hard rule. TABLE (peak dBFS / mono LUFS or file LUFS / corr L-R / corr below 150 Hz / L-R dB / peak share / CLAP margin): shield_light -9.0 / -24.5 / 0.50 / 0.996 / 0.47 / 3.6% / +0.053; shield_medium -5.0 / -20.2 / 0.48 / 0.994 / 0.30 / 6.6% / +0.115; shield_heavy -1.5 / -17.6 / 0.53 / 0.991 / 0.15 / 6.8% / +0.077; fold_jump -1.5 / -20.2 / 0.62 / 0.999 / 0.14 / 8.3% / +0.227; fold_exit -4.0 / -23.8 / 0.62 / 0.994 / 0.27 / 10.3% / +0.251; alarm_shields_down -11.6 peak, -20.0 LUFS, fundamental 418 Hz, nothing above 5 kHz / -0.085 (hint only); cruise_charge -11.1 / -26.5 / 4.8 s, cue 4.0 / +0.014; cruise_loop -10.8 / mono -24.0 / 0.60 / 0.9997 / 0.10 / +0.134; fold_tunnel_loop -18.8 / mono -34.0 / 0.60 / 0.9995 / 0.06 / +0.145; weapon_beam_loop -13.4 / mono -26.0 / 0.60 / 0.989 / 0.03 / -0.009 (hint); mining_laser_loop -17.9 / mono -31.0 / 0.60 / 0.9997 / 0.65 / -0.007 (hint). Energy shares of the mono sum by the rule's whole-file FFT: shields above 1 kHz 0.72-0.76, above 4 kHz 0.45-0.51, below 250 Hz 0.17-0.22; the Welch band table in the json shows lower low shares (0.05 to 0.12) only because Welch down-weights a hit at the very start of a file (the rule itself uses the whole-file FFT). DESCRIBING MODEL (what it answered): shield_light 'a gun being fired with an echo'; shield_medium 'a keyboard being played ... resembling typing on a typewriter'; shield_heavy 'an explosion, specifically a bomb or fireworks'; fold_jump 'a ball bouncing and then hitting something hard'; fold_exit 'a liquid being sprayed and then dripping'; alarm_shields_down 'a video game sound'; cruise_charge 'a dark and spacey synth pad with reverb'; cruise_loop 'an electronic organ with a dark tone playing a long note'; fold_tunnel_loop 'the humming of an engine idling'; beam 'a sine wave'; mining 'music playing in the background'. Reading: the shields and fold sounds are heard as sharp, noisy, energetic events (gun, keyboard clatter, firework, spray), none as a knock on a bowl or a dull blow; the alarm is heard as a video-game sound, which is a worry (see open issues). ALARM ENVELOPES side by side (20 ms per char): shields_down [@@@@@@@@@@@@@@   @@@@@@@@@@@@@@   @@@@@@@@@@@@@@    @@%###**++==--:::.], hull_critical [    @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@%        @@@@@@@@@@@@@@%], missile [  %@@@@@    @@@@@*   %@@@@@    @@@@@*   %@@@@@] (same 20 ms/char), heat (30 ms/char) two long blocks, fuel_low (50 ms/char) one decaying bell, master_caution (10 ms/char) two decaying chimes. Shields_down is the only one with three equal hard blocks and a long fade after them. PICTURES (assets/audio/render/<category>/<id>.png, plus the chain picture): shields: a dense vertical hash from 1 to 10 kHz in the first 100 to 150 ms (hundreds of sparks a second), broad hiss under it whose upper edge sinks over the file, thinning to single vertical sparks (heavy: out to 1.5 s, hiss to about 1 s), a 100 Hz growl line with a sag and a faint 280 Hz line, a low push at the hit; no horizontal ringing hull lines. fold_jump: 0 to 0.45 s the charge's tone stack (110 to 210 Hz) carries on and fades while a hiss band climbs from 1 kHz to 10 kHz, the crack at 0.5 s is a vertical bar from 150 Hz to 14 kHz with a falling 90 to 50 Hz push under it, then the hiss band sinks and sparks thin out, and from about 1.5 s the tunnel drone lines (118, 147, 163, 211 Hz) come up. fold_exit: drone lines at the start fade by 0.6 s, the hiss band climbs 0.4 to 1.05 s, crack plus push at 1.05 s, dense sparks that thin out to 1.7 s, then three vertical bursts with low energy at 1.86, 2.21 and 2.72 s (the metal ticks). alarm: three parallel falling diagonals (1.4 kHz to 700 Hz with 3rd and 5th harmonics above), then a 420 Hz line with harmonic lines up to 4.6 kHz fading. cruise_charge: the first 4 s unchanged, then the drone lets go by about 4.45 s and a 500 Hz whine line hangs to about 4.65 s. Chain picture assets/audio/cache/chain_fold_new.png (charge, jump, tunnel twice, exit): continuous, no hole; level at the joins within 1 dB (charge end -19.9 dB rms, jump start -20.9 dB; jump end -30.7 dB, tunnel start -29.6 dB).

notVerified: Nothing was listened to: I cannot hear. Whether the shields and fold sounds now read as energetic and not as a salad bowl, whether the jump and exit carry the push the owner wants, and whether the alarm now reads as critical is for the owner's ears. The describing model's answers (gun with echo, typewriter, explosion or fireworks, ball hitting a table, liquid spray, video game sound) only say the sounds are sharp and noisy; the alarm answer 'a video game sound' may be a warning sign.
The 30 to 90 Hz flutter of the hiss was checked only statistically (the envelope's 30-90 Hz band holds 29 % against about 12 % for plain noise on the heavy shield), not by ear.

That the hanging whine in the cruise_charge tail sounds like a natural hold rather than a small swell: the head ends with its whine at its lowest (0.05) and the tail brings it up about 5 times over 0.3 s as the drone lets go; judged by numbers and the picture only.
The audition page, the player's early start of the next file in a chain (I assumed 15 ms) and the cabin impulse response were not exercised.
The build wrote into assets/audio/render while the audition page may be serving it; I did not check what the page showed during that.
openIssues: The describing model heard alarm_shields_down as 'a video game sound' and CLAP's margin is negative (-0.085, hint only; best match 'a critical failure warning buzzer descending', worst 'a toy siren'). The three sweeps are very regular (equal length, equal gaps, steady 90 Hz flutter). If the owner still finds it too clean, roughen the timing a little or let the sweeps get shorter and louder toward the third.

The Welch band table in each json (and so the 'lowShare' style numbers) under-reports energy of a hit at the very start of a file (shields show 5 to 12 % below 250 Hz there against 17 to 22 % by the rule's whole-file FFT). measure.py could weight the first segment properly; not my area.

The jump and exit carry the tunnel drone at the loop's level (jump from 1.5 s, exit at the start), so the 'thins into silence' of the jump is really 'thins into the tunnel'. If the player crossfades the files itself this could be removed from the jump and the exit; one line each in cat_drive.py.

The side of the cruise loop, tunnel and beam is built from the tones above 170 Hz (and, for the weapons, above 185 Hz) plus noise; the beam's corr below 150 Hz is 0.989, the closest of all to its limit of 0.98.
